iPadOS 27.2 was released in beta this week, and in addition to introducing the redesigned Health app, Apple has brought over a feature that recently launched on the Mac: a Siri popup when text is selected.

iPadOS 27.2 adds the feature of a Siri popup when text is selected, the same as macOS Golden Gate

Siri AI is the main new feature of iOS 27, iPadOS 27, and related operating systems, and Apple offers many different ways to open this enhanced intelligent assistant.

On the iPad, you can summon Siri with the "Siri" or "Hey Siri" voice commands, swipe down from the top of the screen, use the newly added Siri option in the edit menu, open the new Siri app, or use my personal favorite method: press CMD + Space to open Spotlight, and ask Siri questions there.

However, iPadOS 27.2 adds another method directly ported from the Mac.

In many situations in macOS 27 Golden Gate, when you select a piece of text, a small Siri icon appears at the top-left corner of the selection. When you hover over it with your cursor, it expands to show an "Ask Siri" text input box.

This feature was not available in iPadOS 27 before. But now, if you connect a trackpad to your iPad, iPadOS 27.2 will have the same effect.

As shown in the image above, the new Siri icon starts out small and won't get in your way, but simply hovering over it brings up the "Ask Siri" input box, which is very convenient.

If you don't have a trackpad connected, the full edit menu will still appear when you select text, and you can click in to open Siri. However, using it with a trackpad will be smoother and more seamless.

macOS has many of these small but productivity-enhancing features that can speed up daily operations, which iPadOS has always lacked. So it's exciting to see such a new Mac feature brought to the iPad.

What do you think of the new Siri popup in iPadOS 27.2? Feel free to share in the comment section.
